name: Thin evidence (abstains)
description: The same machinery on a question the bundle cannot answer. The critic refuses to produce a verdict. This is the honesty case. Keep it in the demo.

payload.question: Did this patient fail because of low tumour mutational burden?

payload.message: Bundle contains a VCF only: no labs, no notes, no treatment dates. The clinical line of investigation has nothing to run on. Proceeding with genomics and literature, and flagging the gap.
Assigned: estimate TMB from the VCF.
Assigned: TMB thresholds for this indication.

payload.result: Targeted panel (41 genes), not WES. Panel size below the threshold for a calibrated TMB estimate.

payload.message: I can give you a mutation count, but calling it TMB would be wrong, because a 41-gene panel does not support a per-megabase estimate. Reporting the limitation instead of a number.

payload.finding: TMB is not estimable from this bundle. The VCF comes from a 41-gene targeted panel; calibrated TMB requires whole-exome or a panel above ~1 Mb of coding territory.
Published TMB thresholds vary by assay and indication, and are not transferable across panel sizes. Without the assay used at treatment time, no threshold can be applied.

provenance.sentence: TMB cut-points are assay-specific and require harmonisation before cross-panel comparison.

payload.message: Is there any path to a TMB estimate from what we hold, any way to bound it at all?
No. A bound from 41 genes would be so wide it would include both sides of every published threshold. It would look like an answer without being one.
Both findings are below threshold, there is no clinical trajectory to corroborate against, and the question names a specific cause we cannot measure. Abstaining.

payload.verdict: ABSTAIN. This bundle cannot answer the question. TMB is not estimable from a 41-gene targeted panel, published thresholds are assay-specific and non-transferable, and no clinical trajectory was supplied to corroborate against. To answer it, supply whole-exome sequencing or the TMB value from the assay used at treatment time, plus treatment dates and response assessments.
